purpose: Close ASVS V1.2.2 on the partner webhook path. A partner-registered URL was stored verbatim and later fetched, with no protocol allowlist at registration and none at either place that fetches it, so javascript:, data:, file: and ftp: were all accepted. Reachability was re-established first, and it corrected the earlier record: the fetch the record named has no runtime caller, and the fetch a partner can reach was unnamed.
requiredInvariants: An allowlist of safe schemes, never a denylist of known-bad ones. A denylist would pass every scheme nobody thought of, which is the same shape of defect as the one being fixed.

The check is applied at all three points and the live one is not assumed. Registration refuses at the door; the controller's test endpoint refuses because that is the fetch a partner can actually reach; the dispatcher refuses because a subscription stored before this control existed never passed registration, and refusing at the point of use avoids a data migration.

http stays on the allowlist, and the reason is written down rather than left implied. This requirement is about the scheme being of a safe kind - transport confidentiality is V12 - and narrowing to https alone would break every partner already registered over http, which is a product decision and not this control's to make.

SSRF is not claimed and not implied. Loopback, link-local and private ranges still pass, and the suite asserts that they do, so the boundary is visible in the tests rather than only in prose. V1.3.6 stays FAIL.

A refusal is recorded, not swallowed. The dispatcher returns a failed delivery naming the reason and continues with the remaining subscriptions; the endpoint returns the reason rather than a generic failure.
No partner loses a working subscription. A URL that was safe stays accepted, and a case asserts the guard still fetches a safe URL rather than simply refusing everything.
Registration business logic beyond this validation, 1C, marketing and presentation are not touched. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation, no migration and no new dependency.
acceptance: webhook-url-protocol.spec.ts passes 22 of 22, with fetch replaced so a passing case cannot leave the process and a regression is visible as a call that should not have happened.

Four mutations are caught: removing the guard from the reachable fetch fails 8 of 22, from registration fails 9, removing the allowlist fails 8, and removing it from the dispatcher fails 1 - one case, because the dispatcher has one, because it has no runtime caller.
V1.2.2 revokes on a negative mutation at the matrix level: removing the controller guard rejects the decision.
The matrix rebuilds at applied 332 / rejected 0, PASS 111 to 112 and FAIL 108 to 107, with no other verdict moved.
tsc --noEmit exit 0, node --test scripts/security passes in full, guard=0.
